channel.title: Archetype Original: Servant Leadership Devotional
channel.description: A daily devotional on servant leadership by Bart Paden.

item.title: Kindness for Someone Else's Sake
item.description: David's kindness to Mephibosheth is decided before Mephibosheth ever proves himself.

item.title: Kindness Presumed Upon
item.description: Judging someone for a shared failure and presuming on patience are named as the same posture, not two separate problems.

item.title: A Tender Heart, Put Into Practice
item.description: A tender heart is named as the condition mercy depends on, not something leadership experience should harden away.

item.title: Restoring Gently
item.description: Restoring someone gently and watching your own exposure to the same failure are one instruction.

item.title: Angry That Mercy Was Shown
item.description: Jonah believes the doctrine of mercy completely and still resents it applied to people he resents.

item.title: Choosing Mercy Over the Payback You're Owed
item.description: Joseph holds total leverage over his brothers and chooses not to use it.

item.title: As You Were Forgiven
item.description: Forgiveness is measured against what was received, not against how the current offense feels.

item.title: Mercy as Imitation
item.description: Mercy modeled after the Father is aimed at people unlikely to ever return it.

item.title: Merciful and Just at Once
item.description: God names mercy and justice in the same breath, refusing to trade one for the other.

item.title: What the Lord Requires
item.description: Mercy is stated as a requirement, not a reward for meeting a harder standard first.

item.title: The Integrity of the Upright Guides Them
item.description: Integrity does not just accuse a leader after failure. It guides them before it, and that is where accountability was always meant to begin.

item.title: I Have Sinned Against the Lord
item.description: David does not explain, minimize, or defend. He says one true sentence and lets it stand.

item.title: Whoever Conceals His Transgressions
item.description: The proverb offers a real choice with a real difference in outcome: concealment or confession, and only one of them leads anywhere good.

item.title: The Lord Looks on the Heart
item.description: Samuel looks at Eliab and sees a king. God looks at the same man and sees someone he has already rejected.

item.title: His Eyes Are on the Ways of a Man
item.description: Elihu insists there is no hiding place dark enough to escape being seen, and no delay built into the judgment either.

item.title: The Heart Is Deceitful Above All Things
item.description: Jeremiah names the one witness every avoider trusts completely and warns that it cannot be trusted at all.

item.title: If We Say We Have No Sin
item.description: The claim to be without fault is not innocence. John calls it self-deception.

item.title: Jonah Rose to Flee
item.description: Jonah does not argue with his assignment. He just leaves in the opposite direction.

item.title: You Will Not Call to Account
item.description: Avoiding accountability rarely starts as an argument. It starts as a quiet decision that no one will ever call this to account.

item.title: So I Threw It Into the Fire, and Out Came This Calf
item.description: Aaron's excuse to Moses is the oldest leadership dodge there is: describe the failure as something that happened to you.

item.title: I Am Innocent of the Blood of All
item.description: The accountability you owe to those you lead is only real if you act on it while you still have the chance.

item.title: Search Me
item.description: Accountability to those you lead is completed by accountability to what is actually in you, invited rather than avoided.

item.title: Examples, Not Domineering
item.description: Accountability to those you lead includes accountability for whether you have become what you are asking them to become.

item.title: Do Not Say We Did Not Know
item.description: Claimed ignorance does not hold up against a heart that was actually paying attention.

item.title: Managing Your Own Household First
item.description: Accountability to those you lead in public is only as real as the accountability you already practice at home.

item.title: I Will Not Cease to Pray for You
item.description: Real accountability to those you lead does not expire the moment your authority does.

item.title: Shepherds Who Fed Themselves
item.description: A shepherd who is well fed while the sheep go unattended has failed at the one thing the role was for.

item.title: So That No One Can Blame Us
item.description: The most credible leaders are not the ones who insist they can be trusted. They are the ones who make their trustworthiness checkable.

item.title: Guard the Deposit
item.description: What was entrusted to you in trust must be carried forward in trust, not simply left untouched.

item.title: Use What Was Given
item.description: A gift left unused is still a form of unfaithfulness, even when it looks like humility.

item.title: Stewards, Not Owners
item.description: What was placed in your care was never yours to begin with, and the accountability follows accordingly.

item.title: The Governor Who Refused the Allowance
item.description: The accountability that matters most is the kind no one is checking but you.

item.title: Settling the Account
item.description: Accountability for what you were given includes what you built with it, not only what you protected.

item.title: Much Required
item.description: What was given in trust is what will be required in full.

item.title: Each Will Give Account
item.description: Accountability owed for one's self is a debt no amount of leadership can transfer.

item.title: Nothing Stays Hidden
item.description: Accountability that exists only in public is not accountability at all.

item.title: Our Secret Sins in the Light
item.description: Accountability for a leader's private decisions does not wait for a public moment.

item.title: Achan's Confession
item.description: Accountability offered before it is demanded is what makes an account trustworthy.

item.title: Be Sure Your Sin Will Find You Out
item.description: Accountability does not stay quiet. It surfaces in the record of what a leader actually did.

item.title: Am I My Brother's Keeper
item.description: The people entrusted to a leader remain the leader's accountability, in success and in failure.

item.title: Where Are You
item.description: Accountability begins with whether the leader answers honestly the first time it is asked.

item.title: Whoever Loves Life, Keep Your Tongue
item.description: Guard the tongue not out of fear of what careless words cost, but out of desire for what careful words build.

item.title: How Forceful Are Honest Words
item.description: Words that carry force carry it because they carry truth.

item.title: Do Not Repay Evil for Evil
item.description: The quality of a leader's speech is directly connected to the quality of the life they are building.

item.title: Bless and Do Not Curse
item.description: Genuine presence with another person's joy or grief cannot be replicated by performing the appropriate response.

item.title: Do Not Speak Rashly
item.description: A pause between stimulus and response is where wisdom enters the conversation.

item.title: A Fool Gives Full Vent
item.description: The team that does not have to manage their leader's emotions is free to do the work they were actually hired to do.

item.title: Like a Dog Seizing Ears
item.description: A leader whose involvement is selective carries more weight when they do choose to enter a dispute.

item.title: Gracious Words Pour From the Wise
item.description: Judicious speech flows from a wise heart. It cannot be reliably produced by technique applied on top of an unformed interior.

item.title: Pleasant Words Are Like Honey
item.description: What a leader says consistently affects the health of the people they lead in ways that extend beyond the immediate conversation.
